title: Agreement with the genus of file 06
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and $C$ a
smooth projective curve over
$k$ (or, more generally, a proper smooth connected curve in the sense of
[def-sc-curves] with $\dim H^0(C,\mathcal{O}_C)=1$). Then the genus
$g(C)$ of [def-pc-genus] equals the genus of
[def-sc-genus].

proof.text: Case (a): $C$ is a smooth projective curve over $k$ [def-pc-smooth-projective-curve]. By [def-pc-curve] $C$ is integral, separated and of finite type over $k$, of dimension exactly $1$; by [lem-pc-projective-proper] the projective morphism $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is proper, and it is smooth by hypothesis. Being integral, $C$ is nonempty and irreducible ([def-pc-integral-scheme]), hence connected. So $C$ is a curve over the algebraically closed field $k$ in the sense of [def-sc-curves] (separated, of finite type, of dimension $\leq1$) which is proper, smooth and connected (nonempty, connected, of dimension one). Hence [def-sc-genus] applies to $C$ and gives $g_{\mathrm{sc}}(C)=\dim_kH^1(C,\mathcal O_C)$, the $k$-structure on $H^1$ being the one induced by the structure morphism $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$.

source.place: Definition 0BY7 (label curves-definition-genus): genus of a proper scheme of dimension 1 with H^0 = k

proof.text: Still in case (a): $C$ is geometrically irreducible over $k$, so that [def-pc-genus] applies. An algebraically closed field is separably closed, and $C$ is nonempty and smooth over $k$, so [lem-pc-rational-points-dense] gives a $k$-rational point $\sigma\in C(k)$. Then [prop-pc-xk-integral] (2), applied to $(C,\sigma)$, says that for every field extension $K/k$ the base change $C_K$ is integral, in particular irreducible ([def-pc-integral-scheme]); by [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] $C$ is geometrically irreducible over $k$. Hence [def-pc-genus] defines $g_{\mathrm{pc}}(C)=\dim_kH^1(C,\mathcal O_C)$, with the same $k$-structure.

source.place: Definition 0B9W (label pic-definition-genus): genus of a smooth projective geometrically irreducible curve

proof.text: Conclusion of case (a): by Steps 1 and 2 both genera are the $k$-dimension of the same $k$-vector space $H^1(C,\mathcal O_C)$, so $g_{\mathrm{pc}}(C)=g_{\mathrm{sc}}(C)$. (Stacks, Algebraic Curves, remark after Definition 0BY7: the two definitions agree whenever both apply.)

source.place: Definition 0BY7 and the paragraph following it

proof.text: Case (b): $C$ is a proper smooth connected curve over $k$ in the sense of [def-sc-curves] (the hypothesis $\dim_kH^0(C,\mathcal O_C)=1$ is not used). We show that $C$ is a smooth projective curve over $k$ [def-pc-smooth-projective-curve]; then case (a) applies and gives the claim. $C$ is proper over $k$ of dimension one, so it is projective over $k$ by [lem-sc-proper-dim-one-projective]. By [lem-sc-smooth-regular] every local ring $\mathcal O_{C,P}$ is a domain; hence $C$ is reduced, and no point lies on two distinct irreducible components (the irreducible components through $P$ correspond to the minimal primes of $\mathcal O_{C,P}$, of which a domain has one). Since $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian and $C$ is of finite type over it, $C$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], so it has finitely many irreducible components; they are closed and pairwise disjoint, hence each is open, and as $C$ is connected and nonempty there is exactly one. Thus $C$ is nonempty, reduced and irreducible, i.e. integral [def-pc-integral-scheme]; it is separated and of finite type over $k$ of dimension exactly $1$, so a curve in the sense of [def-pc-curve], smooth and projective over $k$, i.e. a smooth projective curve over $k$ [def-pc-smooth-projective-curve]. Now Steps 1--3 apply to $C$.

split_report.summary: Read def-pc-genus (Stacks 0B9W: dim_k H^1(X,O_X) for a smooth projective geometrically irreducible curve) and def-sc-genus (dim_k H^1(C,O_C) for a proper smooth connected curve over algebraically closed k; Stacks 0BY7, verified in tags/tags and curves.tex). Both genera are dim_k H^1(C,O_C), so the proof is the verification that C satisfies the hypotheses of both definitions: case (a) smooth projective curve: proper (lem-pc-projective-proper), connected, a curve of def-sc-curves (Step 1); geometrically irreducible via a rational point and prop-pc-xk-integral (Step 2); equality (Step 3, elementary). Case (b) proper smooth connected curve: projective (lem-sc-proper-dim-one-projective) and integral (lem-sc-smooth-regular, Noetherian, connected), reducing to case (a) (Step 4); the hypothesis dim H^0 = 1 is not needed (it is automatic, cf. lem-sc-global-functions). Statement unchanged; no new node. The citer lem-sc-pic-proper-ntorsion (step 1) applies the item to a smooth projective geometrically integral curve over algebraically closed k, which case (a) covers.
